newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel says no breakthrough likely at Egypt summit.
newsitem.headline: Israel says no breakthrough likely at Egypt summit.

text.p: Israel forecast that a summit with Egypt on Tuesday on reviving Middle East peacemaking would make only limited progress towards ending a crisis with the Palestinians over Jewish settlement in East Jerusalem.

"I don't expect a dramatic breakthrough but I do expect an inching forward in bridging the gaps between the Palestinian Authority and the Israeli government," David Bar-Illan, a spokesman for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, said on Sunday.
Netanyahu will meet Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak on Tuesday at Egypt's Red Sea resort of Sharm el-Sheikh, his office said after dicussions in Jerusalem with Mubarak envoy Osama el-Baz.

Netanyahu earlier sent out a clear signal he had no intention of stopping the construction of 6,500 homes for Jews at Har Homa, a Jerusalem hilltop that Palestinians call Jabal Abu Ghneim. Bulldozers began work on the site on March 18.

The Palestinians have demanded that Israel must scrap the project before peace negotiations can resume, but Netanyahu, asked on Israel Army Radio about a possible freeze, said: "It is not on the agenda -- not on mine."

Palestinians say the project will complete a ring of Israeli settlements around annexed East Jerusalem, cutting it off from the rest of the West Bank and cementing the Jewish state's hold on all of the city.
Israel captured East Jerusalem in the 1967 Middle East war and says it will never cede any part of the city.
Palestinians want East Jerusalem as capital of a future state and accuse Israel of pre-empting final peace talks at which the city's fate is to be negotiated.

Mubarak has previously suggested halting settlement activity for six months but he told a news conference after meeting Jordan's King Hussein on Saturday that he was sending Baz to Israel without any preconditions.
"I think the Egyptian side prefers to have things ensured beforehand so that they will be certain that there will be something successful in (Tuesday's) talks," Bar-Illan said.
"They (the Egyptians) would have probably preferred that we announce some kind of freeze on construction but we believe that a freeze on construction is like declaring a freeze on life."
Bar-Illan said Israel would stick to its demand that the Palestinian Authority, in charge of areas in the West Bank and Gaza Strip, must do more to curb "terrorism".
Israel stepped up its calls for strident steps against Moslem militants after a March 21 explosion at a Tel Aviv cafe killed the Palestinian bomber and three Israeli women.
Palestinian President Yasser Arafat told reporters in Gaza he hoped the summit would succeed and he said the peace process was a vital Palestinian interest.
But Palestinian Information Minister Yasser Abed Rabbo told Reuters: "We are not optimistic...because of Israel's refusal to halt settlement activities."
